prompt.context: Your client is a chemical company, ChemCo. Due to stagnant growth in the chemicals segment, they decided to create a high growth bio-products segment. This segment sells these products to universities and labs primarily for use in drug development. Revenue for the new segment has been growing at 3-5% per annum for the last few years. The CEO is unhappy with this and wants to achieve 10% growth in revenue in the next year. You have been hired to help bridge this gap and achieve this target.
prompt.question: How can ChemCo achieve 10% revenue growth in the bio-products segment next year?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current revenue of the bio-products segment?
clarifying_info.a: Last year bio-products segment accounted for $300 million in revenue.

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall industry growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: The bio-products industry has been growing at 10%, hence the CEO's target.

exhibits.title: Competitor Revenues and Product Mix
exhibits.shows: A bar chart and table listing competitors (C1, C2, ChemCo, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8) by revenue and number of product categories.

exhibits.title: Industry Revenue against R&D Spend
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot of revenue per category (y-axis, $millions) versus R&D spend per category (x-axis, $millions) for ChemCo and competitors C1–C8, showing a positive relationship between R&D and revenue per category.

data.key_observation: At $6M R&D per category, revenue per category is approximately $70M

framework: Industry analysis: bio-products industry growth rate and trends
Client analysis: current revenue growth vs. industry, product mix, limitations on growth
Growth strategies: geographies, channels, acquisitions, product mix, R&D investment

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what insights can you draw about ChemCo's competitive position and product mix?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should note: ChemCo has the most product categories (20) among all competitors, yet ranks only 3rd in revenue. Competitors with higher revenue (C1, C2) operate with far fewer categories (6 each). ChemCo is over-diversified, which may have caused diseconomies of scope, inefficient allocation of sales/marketing resources, and inefficient R&D spend across too many categories.

questions.prompt: Given the R&D data in Exhibit 2 and the internal breakdown of products, what is the recommended R&D reallocation and what revenue outcome does it project?
questions.guidance: The casebook provides two product buckets: 5 Strategic Products (Revenue=$200M, R&D=$10M) and 15 Non-strategic Products (Revenue=$100M, R&D=$20M). Exhibit 2 shows that $6M R&D per category yields ~$70M revenue per category. Candidate should recommend reinvesting the $20M currently on non-strategic products into strategic products, bringing total R&D on strategic products to $30M ($6M x 5 categories), projecting $350M total from strategic products over 3 years.

math.setup: Current: 5 strategic categories, $10M R&D total ($2M each), $200M revenue. 15 non-strategic categories, $20M R&D total, $100M revenue. Exhibit 2 shows $6M R&D per category → $70M revenue per category.
steps: Reallocate: eliminate R&D on non-strategic products; invest $6M x 5 = $30M in strategic categories
Projected strategic revenue at full ramp: $70M x 5 categories = $350M
Non-strategic revenue declines from $100M to $0 evenly over 5 years (-$20M/year)
Revenue projections: Year 0 = $300M; Year 1 = $330M ($250M strategic + $80M non-strategic); Year 2 = $360M; Year 3 = $390M; Year 4 = $370M; Year 5 = $350M
math.answer: Year 1 total revenue = $330M, a 10% increase over $300M, meeting the CEO's target

questions.prompt: What are the risks with this approach and what next steps would you recommend?
questions.guidance: Risks: analysis only splits products into strategic vs. non-strategic — good individual products within non-strategic bucket may be missed; assumption that R&D is the only factor influencing revenue; if $70M per category is not achieved, growth target will fail. Next steps: investigate revenue and R&D at individual product level for granularity; consider adding a sixth strategic product for future growth but monitor over-diversification risk; conduct competitive analysis to understand which 4-7 product categories competitors focus on.

brainstorming.prompt: What other growth strategies could ChemCo consider beyond R&D reallocation?

categories.name: Geographic Expansion
ideas: Enter new geographic markets where bio-products demand is growing
Target international universities and research labs

categories.name: Channel Expansion
ideas: Develop direct sales force targeting key lab decision-makers
Explore online/catalog channels for smaller volume customers

categories.name: Acquisitions
ideas: Acquire smaller competitors to gain product categories and scale
Acquire companies with complementary R&D pipelines

categories.name: Product Mix Optimization
ideas: Discontinue underperforming non-strategic products faster to redeploy resources
Develop new products in high-growth sub-segments

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Review pricing power on strategic products given their R&D backing
Bundle products for university lab contracts

recommendation: ChemCo should reorganize its R&D efforts to focus on the 5 strategic products, shifting $20M of R&D currently allocated to non-strategic products into strategic categories ($6M per category x 5 = $30M total)

This reallocation is projected to grow Year 1 revenue from $300M to $330M — a 10% increase that meets the CEO's target — with strategic revenue ramping to $350M over 3 years as non-strategic revenue phases out
risks: Assumption that R&D is the primary (only) driver of revenue; other factors may limit actual revenue per category from reaching $70M
Strategic vs. non-strategic classification is coarse — individual high-performing non-strategic products may be unnecessarily abandoned
Revenue decline from non-strategic products ($20M/year) outpaces strategic ramp-up after Year 3, causing total revenue to peak and decline
next_steps: Conduct a product-level analysis of revenue and R&D to refine strategic vs. non-strategic classification
Evaluate adding a sixth strategic product category to sustain long-term growth, while monitoring over-diversification
Perform competitive analysis to benchmark which 4-7 product categories leading competitors (C1, C2) focus on and why
